description: Patient is a retired librarian living alone in a suburban home
presentation: A 62-year-old woman with metastatic breast cancer on checkpoint immunotherapy developed presumed immunotherapy pneumonitis requiring multiple courses of prednisone (each more than 1 month long), most recently completed 2 months ago. She is a retired librarian living alone in a suburban home. A CT chest now shows diffuse bronchial wall thickening and tree-in-bud opacities. She remains dry-coughing and dyspneic off steroids. Patient has a history of positive quantiferon with negative AFB testing x 3 about 5 years prior. What dose of steroids should be restarted and what is an appropriate taper plan?
